scope: Modern unit timelines 1946–present for the 16 Natural Earth admin-0 units of audit regions eastern-europe, russia and central-asia (BGR BLR CZE HUN MDA POL ROU SVK UKR RUS KAZ KAB KGZ TJK TKM UZB). Researched 2026-10-01/02: post-war regime changes and renames (Bulgaria 1946/1990, Romania 1947/1965/1989, Hungary 1946/1949/1989, Poland 1952/1989, Czechoslovakia 1960/1990 and its dissolution 1992/93), the Soviet Union (1946–1990 in tier 0; dissolved 26 December 1991, so its successors appear from 1991), territory that changed hands inside these units (Jäniskoski 1947, the Polish–Soviet exchange of 1951, Crimea 1954/1991/2014, Baikonur lease 1994), breakaway and occupied areas (Chechnya/Ichkeria 1991–1999, Transnistria 1991–, the Donetsk and Luhansk People’s Republics 2014–2021, Russian-held Ukraine 2022– from DeepStateMap year-end snapshots, the Ukrainian-held part of Kursk Oblast 2024, the southern Kurils). De facto control at year end in tier 0; contested areas as tier-1 overlays (0001–0013); editorial decisions, cross-file hand-offs, island problems and known gaps as note entries (0101–0117). Scripts and data in .cache/audit/audit-modern-europe-east-central-asia/. Wikidata ids verified with wbgetentities/wbsearchentities on 2026-10-01/02.

sources.title: 1951 Polish–Soviet territorial exchange (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Signed 15 February 1951, ratified by Poland 28 May and by the USSR 31 May, in force 5 June 1951; about 480 km² each way: Poland gave the Sokal land (Bełz, Krystynopol, Uhnów, the Rawa Ruska–Krystynopol railway) and received part of Drohobych Oblast (Ustrzyki Dolne, Czarna, Lutowiska, Krościenko, Bandrów Narodowy, Bystre, Liskowate).

sources.title: Umowa o zmianie granic z 15 lutego 1951 (Polish Wikipedia)
sources.note: Poland ceded Bełz, Uhnów, Krystynopol, Waręż, Chorobrów and the left-bank part of Sokal (Żwirka); the USSR ceded the lands north-east of the upper San with Ustrzyki Dolne, Czarna, Lutowiska and Krościenko; 480 km².

sources.title: Umowa graniczna pomiędzy Polską a ZSRR z 16 sierpnia 1945 roku — treaty text (Polish Wikisource)
sources.note: Article 2: from the source of the San down the San (mid-stream) to a point south of Solina, then east of Przemyśl and west of Rawa Ruska to the Sołokija river — the line in force until 1951.

sources.title: Umowa o zmianie granic między Polską a ZSRR (1951) — treaty text (Polish Wikisource)
sources.note: Describes the new (today’s) line: in the Lublin section it leaves Uhnów, Bełz, Waręż etc. to the USSR and ends on the Bug; in the Drohobych section it leaves Lutowiska, Bystre, Bandrów-Kolonia, Krościenko and Liskowate to Poland and ends near Jureczkowa/Łopusznica.

sources.title: Oder–Neisse line (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Potsdam (2 August 1945): territories east of the line under Polish administration pending a peace settlement; recognised by East Germany (Zgorzelec, 6 July 1950), accepted by West Germany with reservations (Warsaw, 7 December 1970), final German–Polish Border Treaty 14 November 1990; northern East Prussia with Königsberg annexed by the USSR as Kaliningrad Oblast.

units.notes: Subunit (hand-drawn, approximate): the San from where today’s border leaves the river, past Dwernik and Zatwarnica, down to the point “south of Solina” named in Article 2 of the 1945 agreement, then a straight line north-east to the junction with today’s border near Jureczkowa/Łopusznica, where the 1951 line ends; today’s border (the 1951 treaty line) closes it. Area 498 km² against 480 km² in the sources; Ustrzyki Dolne, Czarna, Lutowiska and Krościenko fall inside, Solina, Zatwarnica and Arłamów outside. The Oder–Neisse territories are shown as Polish from 1946 (de facto Polish administration since 1945) — see note m-europe-east-central-asia-0109.
